app_description: Earthquakes around the world, as they happen.
meaning_at_point: Likely Intensity {roman} ({level}) at the selected point
meaning_at_point_not_felt: Likely not felt at the selected point
og_site_summary: Where it hit, how big it was and what it meant for the places you care about.
globe_label: Globe of Earthquakes. Drag or use the arrow keys to rotate; scroll or press + and − to zoom.
globe_unavailable: Your browser can't draw the globe.
details_sequence_none: No related Earthquakes nearby this week.
details_sequence_largest_one: The largest of a group: {count} struck nearby this week.
details_sequence_largest_other: The largest of a group: {count} struck nearby this week.
details_sequence_fore: Came before a bigger {magnitude} nearby on {date}.
details_sequence_doublet: Struck near an equally strong {magnitude} from {date}.
filter_custom_error_order: The start date must be on or before the end date.
filter_custom_error_future: The end date can't be after today.
summary_area_empty: No earthquakes here in this interval. Try a longer interval or zoom out.
search_empty: No earthquakes near a place with that name. Try a country or region.
about_lead: Earthquakes as ripples through a connected Earth. Every dot on the globe is a recent earthquake, drawn where it started underground. The ones people could feel send a wave across the surface.
about_see_body: Earthquakes from the source you pick, over the last 24 hours, 3 days or week. The last 24 hours refresh every minute. Size is magnitude, colour is depth, the ring around the globe is time.
about_read_body: The likely-felt area is an estimate from magnitude and depth, not observed shaking. Felt reports, when the source has them, are people who said they felt it.
info_summary_likely_felt: Earthquakes whose shaking probably reached people at the surface. It's an estimate from magnitude and depth, not from felt reports.
info_summary_largest: The strongest earthquake so far in this time window, by the magnitude the source reports.
info_filter_time: How far back to look, or a range of dates in UTC. The last 24 hours refresh every minute.
info_filter_magnitude: Hide smaller earthquakes. Magnitude is logarithmic: each whole step releases about 32 times more energy.
info_filter_depth: Where the earthquake started underground. Shallow is above 70 km, mid 70–300 km, deep below 300 km. Shallow ones are usually felt more strongly.
info_filter_source: Which catalogue to show. USGS and EMSC locate and measure earthquakes independently, so their numbers can differ slightly. All shows both and counts an earthquake reported by both once.
info_details_magnitude: The size of the earthquake at its source, as measured by the catalogue. Each whole step is about 32 times more energy.
info_details_depth: How far below the surface the rupture began. Deeper earthquakes spread their shaking wider but weaker.
info_details_likely_felt: How far from the epicentre people were likely to feel it. An estimate from magnitude and depth, not observed shaking.
info_details_felt_reports: How many people told the USGS ‘Did You Feel It?’ survey that they felt this earthquake.
info_details_type: The method used to measure the magnitude. Moment magnitude (Mw) is the most reliable for large earthquakes.
info_details_source: The catalogue that reported this earthquake. The link opens its official event page.
search_locate_denied: Location access is blocked. Allow it in your browser settings to find earthquakes near you.
search_locate_unavailable: Your location isn't available right now. Try again or search a place.
search_locate_empty: No earthquakes in this view to match your location. Try a longer interval.
map_area_caption_24h: In this area in the last 24 hours · {count} · Size = magnitude
map_area_caption_3d: In this area in the last 3 days · {count} · Size = magnitude
map_area_caption_7d: In this area this week · {count} · Size = magnitude
map_area_caption_1y: In this area in the last year · {count} · Size = magnitude
map_area_caption_custom: In this area from {from} to {to} · {count} · Size = magnitude
globe_failed: The globe couldn't load. Reloading the page usually fixes it.
section_blurb: A slice through the ground, west to east, through this earthquake. Relief from ETOPO1 and GMTED2010, layers from CRUST1.0, earthquakes from {source}.
section_blurb_slab: A slice through the ground, west to east, through this earthquake. Relief from ETOPO1 and GMTED2010, layers from CRUST1.0, the top of the sinking plate from USGS Slab2, earthquakes from {source}.
section_footnote: {length} slice through this earthquake, west → east · Top 10 km stretched ×{top} · Below ×{below}
section_error: The slice couldn't load. Check your connection and try again.
section_alt_intro: Cross-section {length} long, west to east, through this earthquake, which started {depth} down {layer}.
section_alt_sea: The sea floor above it lies {depth} below sea level.
section_alt_land: The ground above it is {height} above sea level.
section_alt_slab: The top of the sinking plate lies {depth} below the epicentre.
section_alt_slab_nearby: A sinking plate crosses the slice, but not under the epicentre.
section_alt_no_slab: No sinking plate is mapped along this slice.
section_alt_others_one: {count} other earthquake lies within {distance} of the slice.
section_alt_others_other: {count} other earthquakes lie within {distance} of the slice.
about_source_relief: relief and sea floor in the section, via AWS Terrain Tiles
about_source_crust: crust layers in the section (Laske et al. 2013)
about_source_slab: top of the sinking plate in the section (Hayes et al. 2018)
map_label: Map of Earthquakes. Drag or use the arrow keys to move; scroll or press + and − to zoom.
